title: How to Write Better AI Prompts for Your Personal Finances
summary: Learn how to write better AI prompts to uncover spending trends, track savings goals and gain deeper financial insights from your connected First Internet Bank accounts through MCP.
body_markdown:
#### Summary


Learn how to write clear AI prompts that can help you better understand spending, savings and financial habits using information from your connected First Internet Bank personal accounts.


#### Better AI Prompts Can Lead to Better Personal Financial Insights


If you choose to connect eligible First Internet Bank personal accounts to an AI assistant through[Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://www.firstib.com/personal/ai-driven-banking/) , you’ll gain a new way to explore your financial information. Setting up that connection is entirely optional and requires action on your part. No accounts are connected unless you choose to establish and use the connection.


Once connected, the real value comes from knowing what to ask.


A clear AI prompt can help you understand where your money is going, how your savings are growing and what changes might help you reach your financial goals sooner. You do not need to be an AI expert. You simply need to give the assistant enough direction to understand what you want to learn.


Here’s how to write better AI prompts for your personal finances and get more useful insights from information available through your MCP connection.


**Note: Connecting your First Internet Bank accounts to ChatGPT* or Claude* is completely optional. Accounts are not connected automatically, and customers who do not set up a connection will see no change to their accounts or banking experience.**


#### Better Answers Start with Better Questions


Consider the difference between these two questions:


*“How are my finances looking?”*


*“How has my spending changed over the last 90 days, and what trends should I review more closely?”*


The first question is broad. The second gives the AI assistant a timeframe and a specific area to analyze. That additional context can lead to a more focused, useful response.


Think of it this way: If you were speaking with a financial professional, you would probably provide some background. AI works better when you do the same.


#### Start with What You Want to Accomplish


Before writing your prompt, ask yourself one question:


**What am I trying to understand or decide?**


Maybe you’re trying to save for a vacation, build your emergency fund or get a better handle on where your money is going each month. Whatever you’re working toward, starting with a clear goal makes it easier to ask a useful question.


Instead of:


*“Tell me about my finances.”*


Try:


*“Based on my recent transaction history, what categories account for the most of my monthly spending?”*


The second version gives the AI assistant a job to do, not just a topic to discuss.


#### Include a Timeframe


A timeframe helps narrow the analysis and makes the response easier to evaluate.


- “Compare my spending from the last 30 days with the previous 30 days.”
- “How have my grocery expenses changed this year?”
- “What subscriptions have I paid for over the last six months?”
- “How does my spending this summer compare to the same time last year?”


If the first response is still too broad, shorten the timeframe or focus on a specific category, merchant or account.


#### Keep the Conversation Going


You do not have to fit everything into one perfect prompt. An AI assistant can help you explore a question one step at a time.


For example, you might begin with:


*“Why did I spend more money this month than usual?”*


Then follow with:


*“Which purchases had the biggest impact on that increase?”*


From there, you could ask:


*“Are there any spending habits I should take a closer look at?”*


Each follow-up builds on the information already provided. This can help you move from noticing a trend to understanding what may be driving it.


#### Ask for Comparisons and Patterns


Financial habits are not always obvious when you’re looking at individual transactions. Asking the AI assistant to compare periods or identify patterns can help bring those changes into focus.


- “What has changed the most in my spending over the past 12 months?”
- “When was I most successful at saving money, and what was different during those months?”
- “Have my recurring charges from Amazon Prime, Spotify or YouTube TV increased over time?”
- “What spending patterns stand out in my checking account over the last year?


These prompts can become even more useful when you include a specific category, merchant or account you want the assistant to review.


#### Explore Everyday Financial Scenarios


AI cannot predict what will happen, but it can help you examine your current financial information in the context of a potential decision.


- “Based on my current spending habits, how much could I realistically save each month for a vacation to Hawaii?”
- “If I spend $8,000 on a kitchen remodel, how might that affect my savings?”
- “Could I comfortably afford a $500 monthly car payment based on my spending over the last six months?”
- “What expenses should I review before saving for a downpayment on a home?”


These prompts are not a substitute for professional advice. They can, however, help you identify information worth exploring before making a decision.


#### AI Prompts for Everyday Money Management


Not sure where to begin? Try one of these prompts after choosing to connect an eligible First Internet Bank personal account through MCP.


**Spending and Budgeting**


- “Where am I spending the most money each month?”
- “Which purchases from Amazon, Target or Walmart had the biggest impact on my spending this month?”
- “How much did I spend on dining out and coffee shops over the last 90 days?”
- “If I wanted to save an extra $200 a month, where could I cut back?”


**Subscriptions and Recurring Purchases**


- “How much am I spending on streaming services like Netflix, Hulu and Disney+?”
- “Which subscriptions have increased in price over the last year?”
- “Show me all the recurring charges coming out of my account each month.”
- “Are there any subscriptions I may no longer be using?”


**Shopping and Lifestyle**


- “How much did I spend at Costco, Sam’s Club and grocery stores this month?”
- “How much have I spent on online shopping over the last six months?”
- “Which stores or retailers received most of my money this year?”
- “What nonessential purchases are taking up the biggest share of my budget?”


**Savings and Financial Goals**


- “If I wanted to save an extra $5,000 this year, where could I make the biggest changes?”
- “What’s having the biggest impact on my ability to save money?”
- “If I cut back on purchases from Starbucks and DoorDash, how much more could I save this year?”
- “What changes could help me build my emergency fund faster?”


#### Think of AI as a Financial Research Assistant


MCP does not replace financial expertise or your own judgment. It gives you another way to access and analyze information from your connected accounts.


You remain in control. You decide whether to connect an eligible account, which questions to ask and how to use the information you receive.


The more context you provide, the more focused the response can be. When an answer raises another question, keep asking.


#### Better Questions. More Useful Insights.


Your First Internet Bank accounts tell the story of how you spend, save and manage your money every day. MCP can make that information easier to explore through AI tools you may already use.


With a thoughtful prompt, you can spend less time sorting through transactions and more time understanding what your finances may be telling you.

#### Frequently Asked Questions


##### How do I write a good AI prompt for personal finances?


Start with a specific financial question or goal. Include the account, timeframe and type of insight you’re looking for. For example, instead of asking “How are my finances looking?” try asking “How has my spending changed over the last 90 days?”


##### Can AI analyze my account information through MCP?


Yes. After you choose to connect an eligible First Internet Bank account through MCP, a supported AI assistant can use the connected account information to respond to your prompts. The usefulness of the response will depend in part on how clearly you frame your question.


##### Can I ask follow-up questions?


Yes. Follow-up questions can help you explore spending habits, savings trends or individual transactions in greater detail.


##### Will AI make financial decisions for me?


No. AI responses provide information based on your connected account data. You are responsible for reviewing that information and making your own financial decisions.


##### Do I have to connect my First Internet Bank account to an AI Assistant?


No. Connecting your accounts is entirely optional. MCP only works if you choose to set up a connection between your eligible First Internet Bank personal accounts and a supported AI assistant. No accounts are connected automatically.


##### What types of personal accounts can I analyze using MCP?


Eligible First Internet Bank accounts may include Personal Checking, Personal Money Market and Personal Savings accounts. Account availability and supported AI platforms may vary.


##### Is MCP a replacement for financial advice?


No. MCP can help you access and analyze information from your connected accounts, but it does not replace professional financial, legal, tax or investment advice.
